Writing our system in matrix form, we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14071250/assets/802292289f84a7d69cfaadd91d88d6a4af9560f618dfae6b553fbca16b63cb96.png)
where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14071250/assets/a851d7868235cdaf8cd6914d21b648b3bd7453549748f4bacc3caf5485c17e50.png) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14071250/assets/696a10263a0fe8a52e0da4a413956bb4040220de2c22ae41f76032f7045a5265.png) So, the matrix of the system is ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14071250/assets/c62e0b111e20b925570d7f178ac556293597b071d9aefb821adc70d83afcb91e.png)

Given the system $\mathbf{x}'(t) = A \mathbf{x}(t)+\mathbf{g}(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the solution of the initial value problem can be written as the sum of the homogeneous part and a particular solution:

$$
\mathbf{x}(t) = \underbrace{e^{A(t-t_0)} \, \mathbf{x}(t_0)}_{\text{homogeneous part}} + \underbrace{\int_{t_0}^{t} e^{A(t-s)} \mathbf{g}(s) \, \text{d}s}_{\text{particular solution}},
$$

where $\mathbf x(t_0)$ is the initial condition vector. 

Let's evaluate each part separately:

- First, we find the homogeneous part. We are given that 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14071250/assets/b7b3cf84162533f6b86e3faf8bba17b335ade35acb42d18aa768a5a1db900730.png)
Since the initial conditions are given at $t = t_0 = 0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}x(0) & ={e}^{At}\,x(0) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{3t} & t{e}^{3t} \\ 0 & {e}^{3t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

- Next, we find the particular solution. Notice that 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14071250/assets/5f80485e8a40e46b5c11656dae755f51f7b0617cbe8b4369cf330f329d042283.png)
So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{3(t-s)} & (t-s){e}^{3(t-s)} \\ 0 & {e}^{3(t-s)}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{3(t-s)} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-3s+3t} \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{t}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-3s+3t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\text{d}s \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3s+3t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{s=0}^{s=t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}-\frac{1}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}-\frac{1}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}-\frac{1}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{3t}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14071250/assets/dbce2a7dd9077db8a6e4f85a0b54c9d2563cad3a0ef5a0a98606ca7a4bb5f81f.png)

feedback.worked_solution:
Given the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+g(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the solution of the initial value problem can be written as the sum of the homogeneous part and a particular solution:

$$
x(t)={{{e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}\,x({t}_{0})}_{⏟}}_{\text{homogeneous part}}+{{{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s}_{⏟}}_{\text{particular solution}},
$$

where $x({t}_{0})$ is the initial condition vector. 

Let's evaluate each part separately:

- First, we find the homogeneous part. We are given that ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{5t} & t{e}^{5t} \\ 0 & {e}^{5t}\end{aligned}].$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{A(t-1)}\,x(1) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{5(t-1)} & (t-1){e}^{5(t-1)} \\ 0 & {e}^{5(t-1)}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{5(t-1)} \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

- Next, we find the particular solution. Notice that 

$$
{e}^{A(t-s)}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{5(t-s)} & (t-s){e}^{5(t-s)} \\ 0 & {e}^{5(t-s)}\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{5(t-s)} & (t-s){e}^{5(t-s)} \\ 0 & {e}^{5(t-s)}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{e}^{5s} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{5t} \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{5(t-1)} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{\int }_{1}^{t}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{5t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\text{d}s.\end{aligned}
$$
